title.narrative: Output 8.2. Increased capacity of member States to improve governance and sustainability of social protection systems

description.narrative: The Government of Zambia, in August 2020, through the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Civil Society for Poverty Reduction (CSPR), to strengthen the participation of civil society organizations in the formulation, implementation, and monitoring of social protection programs in Zambia. The partnership has since led to the development of the Social Accountability Facilitators Manual to empower CSOs at district level to undertake social protection budget tracking and service quality audits. This tool was adopted by the Ministry of Community & Social Services in September 2021, and endorsed for national roll-out. CSPR has further launched a Social Protection for Development campaign on 23rd July 2021, to serve as a CSO led social protection advocacy tool in the lead-up to the August national elections. The campaign was able to mobilize a national debate by the political parties competing in the national elections, as well as to undertake an audit of their manifestos to inform the public on how social protection was prioritized and addressed. The ILO has partnered with Civil Society for Poverty Reduction (CSPR) to develop the Social Accountability Facilitators Manual and advance its adoption by Government. The ILO has further supported the design and delivery of the Social Protection for Development Campaign.
